resend.label: Resend
resend.apiKeySet: An API key is already configured. Leave blank to keep it.

test.title: Send a test email

email.comingSoon: More notification options are coming here: custom email templates, send-rate limiting, and per-alert frequency controls.
email.channelsCta: Looking for Slack, Discord, or webhook notifications instead?

wizard.intro: Password resets and alert emails go out through an SMTP server. Enter yours, save, then send a test to a real inbox before moving on.
wizard.others: Using AWS SES or Resend instead?

orphans.title: Leftover resources
orphans.description: Containers, volumes and certificates that no app or database accounts for. They are removed automatically once they stay orphaned past the grace period. Database data volumes are never removed.
orphans.empty: Nothing left over. Every container and volume belongs to a live app or database.

reason.stale_generation: Older release of a live app

toast.dryRun_one: Dry run: {{count}} resource would be removed.
toast.dryRun_other: Dry run: {{count}} resources would be removed.

authEngine.title: Sign-in engine
authEngine.description: Sign-in, sessions, API tokens, two-factor and passkeys run on the auth library {{version}}.

iamTemplates.title: Add a policy from a template
iamTemplates.description: Pick a ready-made policy. You can attach it to a user or token now, or later from the policy list.
iamTemplates.attachIdRequired: Enter the ID to attach to, or choose Nothing yet.

aiControl.title: AI control
aiControl.description: Decide what agents and the built-in assistant may do on this instance. The server enforces this on every request, whatever the token allows.
aiControl.navDescription: Turn agent access off, read-only or on, and limit it to chosen environments.

off.label: Off
off.description: Every agent request is refused. Humans are not affected.

observe.label: Observe
observe.description: Agents can read apps, logs and metrics, but not secrets, and change nothing.

operate.label: Operate
operate.description: Agents can read, write and deploy in the environments below. They cannot use root, change secrets, backups or instance settings.

admin.label: Admin
admin.description: Agents can use any ability their token holds in the environments below. A person must still approve protected deploys.

aiControl.adminUnavailable: Admin mode needs the experimental feature ai-control to be enabled on the server.
aiControl.envKindsDescription: Applies to operate and admin. Apps with no environment count as custom.
aiControl.viewAudit: View agent activity in the audit log

revoke.title: Revoke every agent token?
revoke.description: Every token with an agent label stops working immediately. This cannot be undone. The built-in assistant keeps working.

aiControl.loadFailed: Could not load AI control settings.

tokens.emptyBody: Create a scoped, revocable credential for the CLI, CI, or an MCP integration.
tokens.name: Name

create.title: Create token
create.description: A scoped, revocable credential for the CLI, CI, or an MCP integration.
create.name: Name
create.agentTip: Label the token as issued to an AI agent, for example "Claude Code". The name is shown here and on every audit log entry the token makes, so you can tell agent changes from human ones.
create.rootExclusive: Root cannot be combined with other abilities
create.signInApproveHint: Lets this token show your sign-in codes and approve new browsers from the CLI. Root does not include it and a device login never grants it. It must expire within 30 days and is revoked when you change or reset your password or sign out your other sessions.
create.signInApproveExpiry: A token that approves sign-ins must expire within 30 days
create.signInApproveAgent: A token that approves sign-ins cannot be issued to an agent
create.secretsRevealHint: Lets this token read a secret value, but only when the server allows token reveal (APP_SECRET_REVEAL_TOKENS=on) and the request carries your password. Every reveal is audited. Root does not include it.

hostFirewall.title: Host firewall
hostFirewall.description: Turns this server's ufw firewall on or off. Turning it on first allows SSH, the control plane ports and HTTP/3, so you cannot lock yourself out.
hostFirewall.confirmOnBody: These commands will run on this server, in order. SSH is allowed before the firewall is switched on.
hostFirewall.confirmOffBody: All ports on this server will be reachable again. This runs:
hostFirewall.missingHelp: Install ufw on this server to manage its firewall from here, or use your cloud provider's firewall.
hostFirewall.sshNote: SSH is on a different port? Set APP_FIREWALL_SSH_PORTS on the control plane before turning this on.

email.title: Set up outgoing email
email.description: Password resets and alert emails need an SMTP server. Pick your provider, then send a test.

alerts.title: Set up alerts
alerts.description: Get a Slack, Discord, email, or webhook message when a deploy fails.

backups.title: Add a backup target
backups.description: Point database and volume backups at S3-compatible storage.

team.title: Invite your team
team.description: Give teammates their own accounts instead of sharing yours.

databaseUpgrades.title: Database upgrades
databaseUpgrades.description: The default upgrade policy for every database that does not set its own.
databaseUpgrades.loadFailed: Could not load the platform upgrade policy: {{error}}
databaseUpgrades.formDescription: Databases inherit this until you override them on their Upgrades tab. Only the platform owner can change it.

githubApp.manageAccessHint: Missing a repository? Choose which repositories this app can see on GitHub, then come back.

owner.legend: Who owns the App on GitHub
owner.orgHelp: The organization you want to deploy from. You need permission to create GitHub Apps there.
owner.orgInvalid: Use the organization's login: letters, numbers and hyphens, up to 39 characters.
owner.allowOthers: Allow other accounts and organizations to install it
owner.publicHelp: Any GitHub account or organization can install this App. Pick this when you deploy from several organizations.
owner.privatePersonalHelp: Private: the App can only be installed on your personal account. Choose an organization above, or allow other accounts, to deploy from an organization.
owner.privateOrgHelp: Private: the App can only be installed on this organization. Allow other accounts to also install it on your personal account or other organizations.

preview.title: Review before connecting to GitHub
preview.description: GitHub's own confirmation page only lets you rename the App; everything else below is fixed before your browser leaves this page.
preview.instanceHelp: Leave blank for github.com. Self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server instances work too, e.g. https://github.example.com.
preview.appNameHelp: The one field GitHub itself lets you change on its own confirmation page too.

githubApp.notInstalled: The App was created but has not been installed on an account or organization yet. Finish installing it on GitHub to pick repositories. A private App can only be installed on the account or organization that owns it.

dockerGuard.title: Docker API guard
dockerGuard.description: Every Docker request this control plane makes passes through an allowlist that blocks privileged containers, host namespaces and protected host mounts.

enforce.label: Enforce
enforce.description: Reject requests a rule denies before they reach Docker.

audit.label: Audit
audit.description: Allow everything and record what enforce would deny.

off.label: Off
off.description: No guard. Takes effect after a restart.

dockerGuard.notConfigured: This control plane was started without the guard.
dockerGuard.restartRequired: The saved mode differs from the running one. Restart the control plane to apply it.
dockerGuard.readyToEnforce: Audit mode saw no would-be denials in the last {{days}} days. Enforce is likely safe.
dockerGuard.pinned: The mode is set by APP_DOCKER_GUARD on the server. Unset it to change the mode here.

githubAppOrg.addOrgHelp: GitHub shows the accounts you can install on. Pick the organization. If you are not an owner, GitHub sends the request to its owners.
githubAppOrg.privateTitle: This GitHub App is private, so GitHub only allows it on the account that owns it.
githubAppOrg.privateBody: To add an organization, open the App's Advanced settings, choose Make public (Any account), then come back and press Add organization. Or register a new App owned by the organization.
githubAppOrg.makePublic: Make the App public on GitHub
githubAppOrg.noSlug: This connection was registered before Levelrail could remember the App's install link. Reconnect the App above (or use manual setup) to enable Add organization here.

mobileDevices.description: Phones paired with this server. Each one holds its own expiring token that can read status and restart, deploy or roll back apps. It can never act as root, reveal secrets or approve sign-ins.
mobileDevices.pairFailed: Could not create a pairing code
mobileDevices.pairingHint: Enter this code in the mobile app, or open the link on the phone. It works once and expires at {{time}}.
mobileDevices.emptyDescription: Pair a device to check status and restart, deploy or roll back apps from your phone.
mobileDevices.revokeDescription: The phone loses access at once and has to be paired again.

oauthPage.title: OAuth sign-in
oauthPage.description: Let people sign in with Google, GitHub, Microsoft, or a self-hosted identity provider instead of a password. Every signed-in account has identical access, there are no roles yet.

banner.title: Register the callback URL with each provider first
banner.body: Every provider asks for a redirect (callback) URL when you create its OAuth app. Copy the URL shown in its row exactly, including the scheme, or sign-in fails with a redirect mismatch.

oauthPage.callbackCopyFailed: Could not copy. Select the URL and copy it by hand.

credentials.description: Create an OAuth app at {{provider}} and paste its client ID and secret here.

restrict.title: Who can join
restrict.description: Only new sign-ins from this email domain get an account created automatically. Leave blank to allow any email.
restrict.label: Restrict to email domain (optional)

issuerUrl.label: Issuer URL
issuerUrl.hint: Your identity provider's OIDC issuer, the address /.well-known/openid-configuration is served from.

displayName.label: Display name (optional)
displayName.hint: Shown on the sign-in button as "Continue with ...". Defaults to "SSO".

session.title: Current session

session.accountHelp: The account every action here is attributed to.
session.untilHelp: After this time you are asked to sign in again.

securityPage.title: Security
securityPage.description: Sessions, two-factor authentication, passkeys, and login protection for this account.

banner.title: Sign-in relies on a password alone
banner.body: Turn on two-factor authentication or register a passkey so a leaked password cannot open this dashboard on its own.

generalPage.title: General
generalPage.description: What this instance is running on, how much disk it has left, and which core features are configured.

density.title: Interface density
density.description: Compact fits more on screen. Comfortable adds spacing. Stored in this browser only.

banner.dockerBody: The control plane cannot talk to the Docker engine, so nothing can be deployed or reconciled until it comes back.
banner.secretsBody: Environment secrets cannot be stored until a master key is set for this instance.

emailPage.title: Email
emailPage.description: The backend that sends alert notifications and password-reset links.

banner.title: No email backend is configured
banner.body: Alert emails and password-reset links will not be sent until you pick SMTP, Amazon SES, or Resend below.

channelsPage.title: Notification channels
channelsPage.description: Connect Slack, Discord, Telegram, a generic webhook, or email once, then attach it from any app's deploy notifications.

empty.title: No notification channels connected
empty.body: Connect Slack, Discord, Telegram, a generic webhook, or email once here, then attach it from any app instead of retyping a URL.

banner.none: Nobody will hear about a failed deploy
banner.noneBody: No notification channel is connected, so deploy results and alerts only show up in the dashboard. Connect one to get them where you already are.
banner.allOffBody_one: Your {{count}} connected channel is switched off, so nothing is being delivered. Enable it from its edit dialog.
banner.allOffBody_other: Your {{count}} connected channels are switched off, so nothing is being delivered. Enable one from its edit dialog.

registryPage.title: Registry credentials
registryPage.description: Usernames and passwords for pulling private images with build.type: image, referenced by name from app.yaml.

empty.title: No registry credentials
empty.body: Add a username and password (or access token) to pull private images from a container registry, referenced by name from app.yaml's build.registryCredential field.

banner.expiredBody: Private image pulls using an expired credential will fail on the next deploy. Replace it before then.
banner.expiringBody: Rotate it at the registry and update it here before the date shown in the table.

rail.label: Backup targets summary
rail.statusBody: Runs, coverage and restore drills live on the Backups page.

backupTargetsPage.title: Backup targets
backupTargetsPage.description: S3-compatible buckets connected as backup destinations for managed databases. AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, or any other S3-compatible endpoint.

empty.title: No backup targets connected
empty.body: Connect an S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, or any other S3-compatible endpoint) to use as a backup destination for managed databases.

banner.title: No backup target configured
banner.body: Managed databases have nowhere to send backups until you connect an S3-compatible bucket. Add one before you need a restore.

certificatesPage.title: TLS certificates
certificatesPage.description: Every domain's certificate, automatic or custom, with expiry and a renew action. Use Renew now to force an immediate re-issuance instead of waiting for the next scheduled check.

empty.title: No domains configured yet
empty.body: Add a domain to an app to see its certificate here, automatic or custom.

banner.expiredBody: Visitors to those domains see a browser warning. Use Renew now on the row, or check that the domain still points at this server.
banner.expiringBody: Automatic certificates renew on their own. If one stays in this state, force a renewal from its row.

table.orphaned: Certificate remains from a domain no longer configured on any app

tokensPage.title: API tokens
tokensPage.description: Scoped, revocable credentials for the CLI, CI, and MCP integrations. Session login only mints tokens: a token can never mint or revoke another token on its own behalf.

banner.body: A leaked root token can change anything on this instance. Revoke it and mint a narrower one with an expiry.

usersPage.title: Users
usersPage.description: Everyone with access to this platform, and what each account can do.

empty.title: No users found
empty.body: Invite a teammate or create a user from the actions above.

banner.title_one: {{count}} invite is waiting to be accepted
banner.title_other: {{count}} invites are waiting to be accepted
banner.body: Invitees have no access until they open their link. Copy it again from the pending invites list below if it got lost.

table.label: Users
table.selfEditHint: You cannot edit your own abilities

cliAccessPage.title: CLI access
cliAccessPage.description: Control this instance from your own computer, like aws or gh, not over SSH.
cliAccessPage.ciHint: Running from CI or a script instead of a person at a keyboard? Use an API token, nothing to approve by hand.

banner.title_one: {{count}} CLI login is waiting for approval
banner.title_other: {{count}} CLI logins are waiting for approval
banner.body: Approve it below only if you started it. If the requesting IP looks wrong, deny it.

install.title: Install the CLI on your computer
install.body: Not the server. This is a small client binary for your laptop or CI runner, separate from the control plane install.
install.note: No root needed, installs to ~/.local/bin. macOS and Linux only today; on Windows, run this from WSL.

point.title: Point it at this server
point.body: Set this once per shell or in your shell profile. Every command talks to that address, and defaults to localhost otherwise.

login.title: Log in
login.body: Opens a code here to approve, the same flow gh auth login and aws sso login use: no SSH key, no server port to open. Approval needs a signed-in dashboard session, so it inherits that session's 2FA or passkey.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Every signed-in account has identical access on this platform: no teams or roles yet.
profile.hasPassword: This account signs in with a password.
profile.noPassword: This account has no password set, only OAuth sign-in.

apiExplorerPage.title: API explorer
apiExplorerPage.description: Browse and try every registered HTTP route on this instance, using your current session. Requests fire for real, same as hitting the endpoint with curl.
apiExplorerPage.filterPlaceholder: Filter by path, method, ability, or description
apiExplorerPage.summary: {{count}} routes, {{examples}} with a worked example ({{percent}}%). A route with no description just means its registration has no doc comment above it yet, not that it is unsupported.

importPlatformPage.title: Import from another platform
importPlatformPage.description: Bring apps and databases over from Coolify, Dokploy or CapRover. Databases and volumes start empty, and re-running skips what was already imported.

builtInRegistryPage.title: Container registry
builtInRegistryPage.description: The built-in image registry: a build cache and distribution backend for multi-node deployments, with no external registry to sign up for. It is served over TLS through the embedded ingress and enforces its own login even if the published port is reached directly.

vaultPage.title: Vault
vaultPage.description: Resolve an app.yaml env var's value live from an external HashiCorp Vault instance, as an alternative to this platform's own envelope-encrypted secret storage.

aiAssistantPage.title: AI Assistant
aiAssistantPage.description: Bring your own LLM API key to chat with an assistant that reads logs, metrics, and deploy history through the platform's MCP tools. It always pauses for your approval before any action that changes state.

observabilityPage.title: Observability
observabilityPage.description: Connect your own Grafana to this control plane's metrics.

nodeProvidersPage.title: Cloud node providers
nodeProvidersPage.description: API tokens for creating servers automatically from the Nodes page. Used only to create and inspect VMs, day to day operation never touches SSH.

containersPage.title: Containers
containersPage.description: Every container on this node, whether or not it's managed by this platform.

networkSharesPage.title: Network shares
networkSharesPage.description: NFS and CIFS/SMB exports, mounted as Docker volumes using Docker's own local-driver network passthrough. Attach one as a volume source when configuring an app's volumes.

organizationsPage.title: Organizations
organizationsPage.description: Group related projects under an organization. File a project into one from the project's own detail page.

agentsPage.title: Agents
agentsPage.description: Connect an AI agent to this instance through MCP, and manage the tokens it uses.

firewallPage.title: Firewall
firewallPage.description: Declarative host firewall rules, reconciled onto this node's firewall (ufw).

fields.statusHelp: Whether this control plane can use the App right now.
fields.instanceHelp: The server this connection talks to.

primaryDomain.title: Set a primary domain first
primaryDomain.body: Git providers redirect back to this instance's primary domain for OAuth callbacks and manifest URLs.
primaryDomain.label: Primary domain
primaryDomain.helper: Saved to ingress settings. ACME and email options stay in domain settings.
primaryDomain.saveFailed: Could not set the primary domain.

githubCallback.title: Callback address
githubCallback.body: Automated setup registers a callback at {{url}}. GitHub redirects there for the life of the App, so this instance must be publicly reachable at that address before you continue.
githubCallback.manualHint: No public address? Use manual setup instead.
